answer: Each identity stakes a 60-credit anchor bond in the cedar registry on its sonnet earning a peer median of 2 or better. Grades are public; a median below 2 burns the bond, and refiling costs a fresh 60. A fake risks 60 plus 25 production per sonnet, 85 per epoch; the kth fake still risks 85, since panels are assigned, not chosen. 1,000 fakes risk 60,000 and spend 25,000 per epoch. A grade-farming ring fails: it cannot grade its own sonnets, and assigned panels grade strangers, so mutual upvotes never count. An honest identity files one real sonnet, passes, and keeps its bond.
